g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.byHand: Set up two equations with matching repeating tails, subtract them, and reduce the resulting fraction.
g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.calculator: Check only: after your fraction is written, divide its numerator by its denominator to check the decimal.
g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.showWork: Write the two aligned multiples, their subtraction, and the fraction before and after reducing.
g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.answerForm: Give one fraction in lowest terms, keeping the original sign.
g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.firstStep: Let x equal the decimal. Count the digits under the repeating bar to choose a power of ten.
g8-t1-repeat-block-fraction.check: Do the repeating tails cancel, and does your fraction have the same sign and whole-number part as the decimal?

g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.byHand: Shift past the nonrepeating part, align two repeating tails, and subtract to find an exact fraction.
g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.calculator: Check only: divide your completed fraction to check its nonrepeating prefix and repeating digit.
g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.showWork: Write both multiples of the original decimal, the subtraction equation, and the reduction.
g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.answerForm: Give a fraction in lowest terms and name the two multiples you subtracted.
g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.firstStep: Let x equal the decimal. Shift once past the prefix, then again by the length of the repeating block.
g8-t1-repeat-after-prefix.check: The tails must begin at the same decimal place before subtraction; compare your fraction's decimal with the entire original.

g8-t1-fraction-decimal.byHand: Use long division and track remainders to decide where the decimal ends or begins repeating.
g8-t1-fraction-decimal.calculator: Check only: compare digits afterward; a rounded calculator display cannot identify the full repeating block.
g8-t1-fraction-decimal.showWork: Show division until the remainder becomes zero or repeats, and mark the digits belonging to a repeated remainder.
g8-t1-fraction-decimal.answerForm: Give the exact decimal with its sign; use a bar over the whole repeating block when needed.
g8-t1-fraction-decimal.firstStep: Divide the numerator's magnitude by the denominator, keeping the sign separate while you work.
g8-t1-fraction-decimal.check: Each remainder must be smaller than the denominator. Does the same remainder produce the same next digit?

g8-t1-terminating-fraction.byHand: Use decimal place value to write a fraction, then divide numerator and denominator by common factors.
g8-t1-terminating-fraction.calculator: Check only: divide the simplified fraction afterward to recover the original decimal.
g8-t1-terminating-fraction.showWork: Write the place-value fraction and the common factor used to reduce it.
g8-t1-terminating-fraction.answerForm: Give one fraction in lowest terms, including the correct sign.
g8-t1-terminating-fraction.firstStep: Count the displayed decimal places to choose a denominator that is a power of ten.
g8-t1-terminating-fraction.check: Can any common factor still divide the numerator and denominator? Does the fraction preserve the decimal's size?

g8-t1-root-classification.byHand: Classify every listed number using perfect squares, repeating decimals, or ratios of integers.
g8-t1-root-classification.calculator: Check only: verify square products afterward; do not decide rationality from a rounded decimal display.
g8-t1-root-classification.showWork: Give one reason for each number. For a root, identify an exact integer root or neighboring perfect squares.
g8-t1-root-classification.answerForm: List all irrational numbers and include the rational or irrational classification of every candidate.
g8-t1-root-classification.firstStep: For each square root, ask whether its radicand is the square of an integer.
g8-t1-root-classification.check: Have you checked every candidate, including negative roots, fractions, and repeating decimals?

g8-t1-number-set-membership.byHand: Decide the number's type and use the nesting of number sets to include every set it belongs to.
g8-t1-number-set-membership.calculator: No calculator needed; use definitions and exact number properties, not a decimal approximation.
g8-t1-number-set-membership.showWork: Write one sentence explaining the number's most specific listed set and why any smaller listed sets do not apply.
g8-t1-number-set-membership.answerForm: List every applicable set from the prompt; use its convention that natural numbers begin at one.
g8-t1-number-set-membership.firstStep: Ask whether the value is a positive counting number, zero, a negative integer, a noninteger fraction, or an irrational root.
g8-t1-number-set-membership.check: If you named a smaller set, did you also include all larger sets containing it?

g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.byHand: Use each stated infinite pattern to decide whether a fixed block repeats forever.
g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.calculator: Do not use a calculator; a finite display cannot establish an infinite decimal pattern.
g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.showWork: Give a separate reason for A and B, addressing termination and whether one fixed block repeats.
g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.answerForm: Label both decimals rational or irrational, with a sentence supporting each label.
g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.firstStep: Underline what stays the same or changes in the gaps between nonzero digits.
g8-t1-infinite-decimal-classification.check: Does your reason use the rule for all future digits, rather than only the first few digits?

g8-t1-root-bounds.byHand: Find consecutive whole numbers whose squares lie on opposite sides of the radicand.
g8-t1-root-bounds.calculator: Check only: after choosing bounds by hand, you may check their squares or the root's approximate location.
g8-t1-root-bounds.showWork: Write both square calculations, the inequality between squares, and the corresponding root inequality.
g8-t1-root-bounds.answerForm: Fill both blanks with consecutive whole numbers in increasing order.
g8-t1-root-bounds.firstStep: Find a perfect square just below the radicand, then try the next whole number's square.
g8-t1-root-bounds.check: Are the bounds one apart, with the radicand strictly between their squares?

g8-t1-order-and-plot.byHand: Convert the rational numbers to comparable forms, bound the root, and place and label every number on the line.
g8-t1-order-and-plot.calculator: Allowed after writing root bounds: approximate the root for comparison and plotting; keep original forms in the final order.
g8-t1-order-and-plot.showWork: Record the comparable values and root bounds or estimate, then label all four plotted positions.
g8-t1-order-and-plot.answerForm: Write a least-to-greatest inequality using the original numbers and give a labeled approximate number-line plot.
g8-t1-order-and-plot.firstStep: Rewrite the mixed number and repeating decimal as whole-number parts plus fractions or decimal values.
g8-t1-order-and-plot.check: Do the labels run left to right in your written order, and does the root lie between its whole-number bounds?

g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.byHand: Compare the positive magnitudes, then use their positions on the negative side of a number line.
g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.calculator: Check only: verify your squared values or approximate the two numbers after deciding the comparison by hand.
g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.showWork: Write a comparison of the positive magnitudes and explain how negating both numbers changes their order.
g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.answerForm: Insert the correct inequality symbol and give one sentence explaining the effect of the negative signs.
g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.firstStep: Temporarily ignore the negative signs and compare the radicand with the square of the positive decimal.
g8-t1-negative-root-comparison.check: Of two negative numbers, is the number with greater magnitude farther left in your comparison?

g8-t1-evaluate-roots.byHand: Find the integer factors that square or cube to each radicand and determine each root's sign.
g8-t1-evaluate-roots.calculator: Check only: square or cube your answers afterward to verify the original radicands.
g8-t1-evaluate-roots.showWork: Write one multiplication or power equality for each root and explain the principal square-root convention.
g8-t1-evaluate-roots.answerForm: Give both integer values in prompt order; the square-root value must follow the principal-root convention.
g8-t1-evaluate-roots.firstStep: Look for equal integer factors: two factors for the square root and three for the cube root.
g8-t1-evaluate-roots.check: Does squaring or cubing recover the radicand, and does the cube-root sign match its radicand?

g8-t1-square-cube-categories.byHand: Test each number separately for being an integer square and an integer cube.
g8-t1-square-cube-categories.calculator: Check only: verify your integer powers afterward; do not rely on rounded root displays.
g8-t1-square-cube-categories.showWork: For each number, give an integer power equality when it fits, or neighboring powers when it does not.
g8-t1-square-cube-categories.answerForm: Label every number square only, cube only, both, or neither, with evidence for both tests.
g8-t1-square-cube-categories.firstStep: Make two columns, square and cube, and compare each number with nearby integer powers.
g8-t1-square-cube-categories.check: Did you test both properties before choosing a category, including for zero or one if either appears?

g8-t1-cube-edge-context.byHand: Use the cube volume to find one edge length, then model the row as that length repeated.
g8-t1-cube-edge-context.calculator: Check only: cube your edge and check the final multiplication after solving by hand.
g8-t1-cube-edge-context.showWork: Write the cube-root calculation and a multiplication for the total row length.
g8-t1-cube-edge-context.answerForm: Give the row length with centimeters as the unit.
g8-t1-cube-edge-context.firstStep: Let s be one cube's edge length and write s cubed equal to the given volume.
g8-t1-cube-edge-context.check: Does cubing one edge recover the volume, and is the row length greater than one edge?

g8-t1-square-equation.byHand: Isolate the squared variable, then decide how many real values can have that square.
g8-t1-square-equation.calculator: Check only: substitute your proposed values afterward; retain exact integers or radicals instead of decimal approximations.
g8-t1-square-equation.showWork: Write each operation used to isolate the square and explain the number of real solutions.
g8-t1-square-equation.answerForm: List all real solutions exactly, or state that there are no real solutions; do not round radicals.
g8-t1-square-equation.firstStep: If there is an added constant or coefficient, undo those operations before taking a square root.
g8-t1-square-equation.check: Substitute each value into the original equation. Have you considered the sign and zero cases for a square?

g8-t1-cube-equation.byHand: Undo cubing with a cube root and determine the solution's sign from the original equation.
g8-t1-cube-equation.calculator: Check only: cube an integer answer afterward or approximate a radical to check its size; keep the answer exact.
g8-t1-cube-equation.showWork: Write the cube-root step and either an integer cube equality or the exact radical form.
g8-t1-cube-equation.answerForm: Give the variable's exact integer or radical value, including its sign.
g8-t1-cube-equation.firstStep: Ask which real number, cubed, equals the right side; a cube keeps the sign of its base.
g8-t1-cube-equation.check: Does cubing your expression reproduce both the size and sign of the right side?

g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.byHand: Model the cube's volume using an edge length, then use the shape of a face to identify its dimensions.
g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.calculator: Check only: verify an integer cube or estimate a radical afterward; do not replace an exact radical with a decimal.
g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.showWork: Write the volume equation, solve for the positive edge length, and connect that length to both face dimensions.
g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.answerForm: Give two equal positive dimensions in centimeters, using exact integers or radicals.
g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.firstStep: Name the edge length s and write a power equation using the given volume.
g8-t1-cube-face-dimensions.check: Are both face dimensions equal and positive, and does their edge length cubed recover the volume?

g8-t1-product-of-powers.byHand: Keep the common base and apply the product rule to the signed exponents.
g8-t1-product-of-powers.calculator: Check only: verify the exponent arithmetic after writing and simplifying it by hand.
g8-t1-product-of-powers.showWork: Write one power with the exponent sum, then simplify that sum, keeping negative signs visible.
g8-t1-product-of-powers.answerForm: Give one power of the original base; a zero or negative exponent may remain.
g8-t1-product-of-powers.firstStep: Check that all bases match, then copy the exponents into an addition expression.
g8-t1-product-of-powers.check: Did you add the exponents while keeping the base unchanged? Recheck every negative term.

g8-t1-power-of-power.byHand: Keep the original base and apply the power-of-a-power rule to both signed exponents.
g8-t1-power-of-power.calculator: Check only: verify the exponent multiplication after doing the rule and arithmetic by hand.
g8-t1-power-of-power.showWork: Write the product of the inner and outer exponents, then simplify it.
g8-t1-power-of-power.answerForm: Give one power of the original base; a negative exponent may remain.
g8-t1-power-of-power.firstStep: Identify the exponent inside the parentheses and the exponent outside them.
g8-t1-power-of-power.check: Does the sign of your exponent match the product of the two original exponent signs?

g8-t1-power-of-product.byHand: Use the common exponent to combine the bases into one integer base.
g8-t1-power-of-product.calculator: Check only: verify the base multiplication after forming the single power by hand.
g8-t1-power-of-product.showWork: Write the product of the bases inside parentheses with the common exponent, then multiply only the bases.
g8-t1-power-of-product.answerForm: Give a single power with an integer base; do not evaluate the whole power.
g8-t1-power-of-product.firstStep: Confirm that the two exponents are equal and copy that exponent unchanged.
g8-t1-power-of-product.check: Did you multiply the bases while leaving the shared exponent unchanged?

g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.byHand: Keep the common base and subtract the denominator's exponent from the numerator's exponent.
g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.calculator: Check only: verify the signed subtraction after setting up and simplifying it by hand.
g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.showWork: Write the exponent subtraction with parentheses around a negative denominator exponent, then simplify.
g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.answerForm: Give one power of the original base; a zero or negative exponent may remain.
g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.firstStep: Copy the numerator exponent first, followed by subtraction of the entire denominator exponent.
g8-t1-quotient-of-powers.check: If the denominator exponent is negative, did subtracting it become addition?

g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.byHand: Rewrite the negative power as a reciprocal and keep track of the separate coefficient.
g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.calculator: Check only: after rewriting, test both expressions at the same positive base value other than one.
g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.showWork: Write the reciprocal identity for the variable power, then multiply by the original coefficient.
g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.answerForm: Give an equivalent expression with only positive exponents and the correct coefficient sign.
g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.firstStep: Separate the coefficient from the variable power; the negative exponent belongs only to that power.
g8-t1-negative-power-reciprocal.check: Is the coefficient still multiplying the reciprocal, and do both expressions agree at a positive test value other than one?

g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.byHand: Simplify the reciprocal first, combine the powers, then rewrite any remaining negative exponent.
g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.calculator: Check only: compare both completed forms at the same positive base value other than one.
g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.showWork: Write the reciprocal rewrite, the combined exponent, and a final form with no negative exponents.
g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.answerForm: Give both requested forms: one power and an equivalent form without negative exponents.
g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.firstStep: Rewrite the negative power in the denominator as a reciprocal before combining the factors.
g8-t1-negative-power-denominator.check: Do your two forms have the same value? If the combined exponent is zero, use the nonzero-base zero-power rule.

g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.byHand: Rewrite zero and negative powers, substitute the given values, and combine the resulting exact terms.
g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.calculator: Check only: evaluate the original expression afterward, using parentheses around negative substituted values.
g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.showWork: Show the power rewrites, substitutions, common denominator, and reduction of the final fraction.
g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.answerForm: Give an exact integer or fraction in lowest terms; do not round.
g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.firstStep: Use the nonzero conditions to rewrite the zero power and the reciprocal square before substituting.
g8-t1-evaluate-zero-negative-powers.check: Is the squared denominator positive, and have you kept the coefficient's sign when adding?

g8-t1-estimate-large.byHand: Identify the first two significant digits, round to one significant digit, and determine the power of ten.
g8-t1-estimate-large.calculator: Check only: convert your completed estimate to ordinary notation afterward to compare its size with the original.
g8-t1-estimate-large.showWork: Mark the rounding digit and write the rounded ordinary number or a decimal-shift step.
g8-t1-estimate-large.answerForm: Give one nonzero digit times a power of ten as an estimate of the record count.
g8-t1-estimate-large.firstStep: Locate the first nonzero digit and the digit immediately after it.
g8-t1-estimate-large.check: Is the coefficient a single digit? If rounding created an extra place, did you adjust the exponent?

g8-t1-estimate-small.byHand: Locate the first nonzero decimal digit, round using the next digit, and determine its place value.
g8-t1-estimate-small.calculator: Check only: convert the completed estimate back to a decimal to compare magnitudes.
g8-t1-estimate-small.showWork: Mark the significant digits used for rounding and show how their place value sets the exponent.
g8-t1-estimate-small.answerForm: Give a single nonzero digit times a power of ten, followed by meters.
g8-t1-estimate-small.firstStep: Ignore leading zeros when locating significant digits, but count their places when finding the exponent.
g8-t1-estimate-small.check: Does your estimate remain a small positive measurement, with one significant digit and the correct unit?

g8-t1-estimated-ratio.byHand: Round each count first, then write the red estimate divided by the blue estimate.
g8-t1-estimated-ratio.calculator: Allowed only after writing both rounded counts and their quotient; use it for arithmetic on those estimates.
g8-t1-estimated-ratio.showWork: Write both one-digit estimates, the coefficient quotient, and the power-of-ten calculation.
g8-t1-estimated-ratio.answerForm: State about how many times as large the red count is; label the result as an estimate.
g8-t1-estimated-ratio.firstStep: Find the first two significant digits of each count and round each count separately.
g8-t1-estimated-ratio.check: Did you divide in the requested order and use rounded counts, rather than round the exact final quotient?

g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.byHand: Move the decimal to form a coefficient between one and ten and count the places moved.
g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.calculator: Check only: evaluate your completed scientific notation afterward to recover the original number.
g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.showWork: Write the coefficient and record the direction and number of decimal places moved.
g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.answerForm: Give normalized scientific notation with every nonzero digit preserved and no rounding.
g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.firstStep: Place a decimal point immediately after the first nonzero digit.
g8-t1-large-scientific-notation.check: Is the coefficient at least one and less than ten, and does expanding the power restore the original?

g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.byHand: Form a coefficient between one and ten, then determine the power needed to preserve the small measurement.
g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.calculator: Check only: convert your completed expression back to a decimal after choosing the coefficient and exponent.
g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.showWork: Record the decimal shift and explain the exponent's sign.
g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.answerForm: Give normalized scientific notation without rounding, followed by millimeters.
g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.firstStep: Locate the first nonzero digit and move the decimal immediately after it.
g8-t1-small-scientific-notation.check: Does the power of ten make the coefficient small enough to match the original width? Keep the unit.

g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.byHand: Use the exponent's sign and magnitude to shift the decimal point and insert zeros as needed.
g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.calculator: Check only: compare your completed decimal with a calculator evaluation afterward.
g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.showWork: State the shift direction and number of places, or mark the decimal's moves on paper.
g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.answerForm: Write the exact number in ordinary decimal notation, without a power of ten or rounding.
g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.firstStep: Decide whether multiplying by the displayed power of ten makes the coefficient larger or smaller.
g8-t1-scientific-to-decimal.check: Does the result's size match the exponent's sign, and are all coefficient digits still in their original order?

g8-t1-scientific-product.byHand: Separate coefficient multiplication from the power-of-ten rule, then normalize the result.
g8-t1-scientific-product.calculator: Allowed after writing the coefficient product and exponent sum; use it for coefficient arithmetic, not the exponent rule.
g8-t1-scientific-product.showWork: Write the coefficient product, exponent sum, and any paired coefficient-and-exponent adjustment.
g8-t1-scientific-product.answerForm: Give exact normalized scientific notation; keep all result digits and do not round.
g8-t1-scientific-product.firstStep: Group the two decimal coefficients together and the two powers of ten together.
g8-t1-scientific-product.check: Is the final coefficient at least one and less than ten? Did every decimal shift have a compensating exponent change?

g8-t1-scientific-quotient.byHand: Write a coefficient quotient and an exponent difference, then normalize the result.
g8-t1-scientific-quotient.calculator: Allowed after writing both operations; use it to divide coefficients and keep the terminating decimal exact.
g8-t1-scientific-quotient.showWork: Show the coefficient division, numerator exponent minus denominator exponent, and normalization.
g8-t1-scientific-quotient.answerForm: Give normalized scientific notation without rounding.
g8-t1-scientific-quotient.firstStep: Keep numerator and denominator order the same in the coefficient division and exponent subtraction.
g8-t1-scientific-quotient.check: Multiply your result by the original divisor. Does it recover the original dividend?

g8-t1-scientific-sum.byHand: Rewrite both quantities with the same power of ten, add coefficients, then normalize.
g8-t1-scientific-sum.calculator: Allowed after writing equivalent terms with a common power; use it for coefficient addition.
g8-t1-scientific-sum.showWork: Show the common-power rewrite, the coefficient sum, and the normalized result.
g8-t1-scientific-sum.answerForm: Give exact normalized scientific notation without rounding.
g8-t1-scientific-sum.firstStep: Choose one displayed power of ten and rewrite the other term to use that power.
g8-t1-scientific-sum.check: Did the rewrites preserve each quantity? The sum should be larger than either positive addend.

g8-t1-scientific-difference.byHand: Rewrite both quantities with a common power of ten, subtract in prompt order, then normalize.
g8-t1-scientific-difference.calculator: Allowed after the common-power rewrite is on paper; use it for the coefficient subtraction.
g8-t1-scientific-difference.showWork: Write the equivalent common-power terms, coefficient difference, and final normalization.
g8-t1-scientific-difference.answerForm: Give exact normalized scientific notation without rounding.
g8-t1-scientific-difference.firstStep: Choose a common exponent and adjust the other coefficient so its value stays unchanged.
g8-t1-scientific-difference.check: Add the subtracted quantity back to your result. Does it restore the first quantity?

g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.byHand: Model the first project's total, then write a quotient comparing that total with the second project's total.
g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.calculator: Allowed after both operations and power-of-ten steps are written; use it for coefficient arithmetic and exact division.
g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.showWork: Show file count times file size, normalization of the total, and the quotient of the two totals.
g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.answerForm: Give the first total in normalized scientific notation with bytes, then an exact times-as-large comparison.
g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.firstStep: Separate the amount in one file from the amount in all files before comparing projects.
g8-t1-model-storage-comparison.check: Did you compare totals? Multiplying the second total by your ratio should recover the first total.

g8-t1-model-square-covering.byHand: Find one panel's side from its area, model the total perimeter, and separately model the combined area.
g8-t1-model-square-covering.calculator: Allowed after writing the root and both total expressions; use it for multiplication and to check the square root.
g8-t1-model-square-covering.showWork: Show the side-length root, one panel's perimeter, total strip length, and total area conversion.
g8-t1-model-square-covering.answerForm: Give strip length in the stated length unit and combined area in normalized scientific notation with squared units.
g8-t1-model-square-covering.firstStep: Sketch one square and label its unknown side; relate the side squared to its given area.
g8-t1-model-square-covering.check: Did you include all four sides of every separate panel and keep length units distinct from area units?

g8-t2-combine-terms.byHand: Combine like variable terms, then undo the remaining operations while keeping both sides equal.
g8-t2-combine-terms.calculator: Check only: substitute your completed solution into the original equation afterward.
g8-t2-combine-terms.showWork: Write the combined equation and a new line for each operation used to isolate the variable.
g8-t2-combine-terms.answerForm: State the variable equal to its exact value.
g8-t2-combine-terms.firstStep: Mark the terms containing the variable; add their coefficients while keeping the constant separate.
g8-t2-combine-terms.check: Does your value make the two sides of the original equation equal, before terms are combined?

g8-t2-perimeter-equation.byHand: Represent all four rectangle sides in a perimeter equation, solve it, then find both dimensions.
g8-t2-perimeter-equation.calculator: Check only: verify the four-side total after writing and solving your equation by hand.
g8-t2-perimeter-equation.showWork: Write the perimeter equation, combine terms, show each solving step, and substitute for the length.
g8-t2-perimeter-equation.answerForm: Give the variable's value and label both width and length in centimeters.
g8-t2-perimeter-equation.firstStep: Sketch the rectangle and label each pair of opposite sides with its given expression.
g8-t2-perimeter-equation.check: Are both lengths positive, and does twice the length plus twice the width match the given perimeter?

g8-t2-both-sides.byHand: Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other, using equal operations on both sides.
g8-t2-both-sides.calculator: Check only: evaluate both original sides with your solution after completing the algebra.
g8-t2-both-sides.showWork: Write a new equivalent equation for each subtraction, addition, or division used to isolate the variable.
g8-t2-both-sides.answerForm: State the variable equal to its exact value.
g8-t2-both-sides.firstStep: Choose one variable term to subtract from both sides; copy its sign carefully.
g8-t2-both-sides.check: Substitute into the original equation. Do both sides give the same number?

g8-t2-equal-savings.byHand: Write each person's savings as starting amount plus weekly savings, set the expressions equal, and solve.
g8-t2-equal-savings.calculator: Check only: evaluate both savings expressions afterward to verify the week and common amount.
g8-t2-equal-savings.showWork: Define your variable, write the equality, show the solving steps, and substitute to find the common amount.
g8-t2-equal-savings.answerForm: Give the number of weeks and the dollar amount each person has then.
g8-t2-equal-savings.firstStep: Let the variable count weeks, and write one starting-amount-plus-rate expression for each person.
g8-t2-equal-savings.check: Is the time nonnegative, and do both expressions give the same dollar amount at that time?

g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.byHand: Distribute on both sides, combine terms, and solve the resulting equation.
g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.calculator: Check only: substitute your final value into the original parenthesized equation afterward.
g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.showWork: Write the fully distributed equation and each operation that gathers terms and isolates the variable.
g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.answerForm: State the variable equal to its exact value.
g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.firstStep: Multiply each outside factor by every term inside its own parentheses.
g8-t2-distribute-both-sides.check: Did distribution reach both terms in each group? Verify your value in the original equation.

g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.byHand: Clear the denominators with a common multiple, distribute, and solve using exact arithmetic.
g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.calculator: Check only: evaluate both original fractions afterward; keep an exact fraction as your solution when needed.
g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.showWork: Write the multiplication that clears denominators, the distributed equation, and the steps to isolate the variable.
g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.answerForm: Give the variable's value as an integer or fraction in lowest terms, without rounding.
g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.firstStep: Find a common multiple of both denominators and multiply the whole of each side by it.
g8-t2-fraction-both-sides.check: Substitute into both original numerators before dividing. Are the resulting fractions equal?

g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.byHand: Distribute the negative factor to the entire group, combine like terms, and solve.
g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.calculator: Check only: evaluate the original expression with your final value after finishing the algebra.
g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.showWork: Show both products from the negative distribution, the combined equation, and the steps isolating the variable.
g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.answerForm: State the variable equal to its exact value.
g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.firstStep: Treat the subtraction before the parentheses as part of the factor multiplying every inside term.
g8-t2-multistep-subtraction.check: Have both inside terms received the negative factor? Does substitution reproduce the original right side?

g8-t2-decimal-equation.byHand: Clear decimals by multiplying every term by the same power of ten, then solve the equivalent equation.
g8-t2-decimal-equation.calculator: Check only: substitute your solution into the original decimal equation afterward.
g8-t2-decimal-equation.showWork: Write the equation with integer coefficients and constants, then each step used to collect terms and isolate the variable.
g8-t2-decimal-equation.answerForm: State the exact variable value without rounding.
g8-t2-decimal-equation.firstStep: Count decimal places and choose a power of ten that makes every coefficient and constant an integer.
g8-t2-decimal-equation.check: Did you multiply every term on both sides? Does the result satisfy the original decimal equation?

g8-t2-classify-solutions.byHand: Distribute and collect terms, then interpret whether the simplified equation determines a value or a constant statement.
g8-t2-classify-solutions.calculator: Check only: verify arithmetic afterward; decide the solution type from your algebra.
g8-t2-classify-solutions.showWork: Show the distributed equation, the simplified result, and a sentence explaining what that result means.
g8-t2-classify-solutions.answerForm: State one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions; if there is one, give its exact value.
g8-t2-classify-solutions.firstStep: Expand the parentheses and compare the variable coefficients on both sides.
g8-t2-classify-solutions.check: If variable terms cancel, is the remaining statement true or false? If they do not, check your solved value.

g8-t2-make-solution-type.byHand: Expand the left side and cancel matching variable terms to find what the constant k must satisfy.
g8-t2-make-solution-type.calculator: Check only: verify the constant multiplication after deriving the condition on k.
g8-t2-make-solution-type.showWork: Write the distributed equation, the equality left after cancellation, and why your chosen k gives the requested type.
g8-t2-make-solution-type.answerForm: Give one valid value of k and describe all values of k that work.
g8-t2-make-solution-type.firstStep: Distribute the outside factor, then subtract the common variable term from both sides.
g8-t2-make-solution-type.check: With your k, is the remaining constant equality always true or always false as the requested type requires?

g8-t2-printing-plans.byHand: Write each plan's cost rule, solve where the costs match, and compare costs at the requested nearby quantity.
g8-t2-printing-plans.calculator: Allowed after writing both rules and solving their equality by hand; use it to evaluate the comparison costs.
g8-t2-printing-plans.showWork: Define the pack variable, show the equality and solving steps, then write both costs at the requested pack count.
g8-t2-printing-plans.answerForm: Give the equation, matching number of packs, and cheaper plan at the specified nearby count.
g8-t2-printing-plans.firstStep: For each plan, separate any setup fee from the charge multiplied by the number of packs.
g8-t2-printing-plans.check: Do the costs match at your solution? Did you compare one pack above or below it exactly as requested?

g8-t2-container-capacity.byHand: Translate both piece counts into expressions, set them equal, and simplify before interpreting the allowed item counts.
g8-t2-container-capacity.calculator: Check only: verify the fixed-piece arithmetic after modeling and simplifying by hand.
g8-t2-container-capacity.showWork: Write both total-piece expressions, their equality, and the constant statement left after variable terms cancel.
g8-t2-container-capacity.answerForm: State one, every, or no allowed x value and explain; allowed item counts are nonnegative whole numbers.
g8-t2-container-capacity.firstStep: For the shelf description, multiply the number of shelves by everything counted on each shelf.
g8-t2-container-capacity.check: Did you count both items and labels, and does your conclusion apply to all allowed item counts?

g8-t2-compare-table-equation.byHand: Find the table's output per minute, identify the equation's rate, and subtract the smaller rate from the larger.
g8-t2-compare-table-equation.calculator: Check only: verify the rate division and difference afterward; preserve exact fractions rather than rounded decimals.
g8-t2-compare-table-equation.showWork: Write the table's output-to-time ratio, the equation's coefficient, and an exact difference of rates.
g8-t2-compare-table-equation.answerForm: Name the faster machine and give the exact difference with production units per minute.
g8-t2-compare-table-equation.firstStep: Choose a table row and divide its production by its elapsed minutes.
g8-t2-compare-table-equation.check: Does another table row give the same unit rate, and is your reported difference positive?

g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.byHand: Read a graph point, calculate hose A's unit rate, compare it with B's rate, and model the total difference.
g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.calculator: Allowed after writing the exact rate difference and time multiplication; use it for arithmetic without rounding fractions.
g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.showWork: Write the point's coordinates, liters divided by minutes, the rate difference, and its product with the stated time.
g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.answerForm: Name the faster hose and give the exact extra liters it adds over the requested time.
g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.firstStep: Read the axis scales, then divide the labeled point's liters by its minutes.
g8-t2-compare-graph-rate.check: Did you multiply the rate difference by time, so the final unit is liters rather than liters per minute?

g8-t2-slope-points.byHand: Read both coordinates and calculate vertical change divided by horizontal change in a consistent point order.
g8-t2-slope-points.calculator: Check only: verify coordinate subtraction or fraction reduction after computing the slope by hand.
g8-t2-slope-points.showWork: List both ordered pairs and write the two coordinate differences in the slope fraction.
g8-t2-slope-points.answerForm: Give the slope as a reduced fraction or integer and explain its sign from left-to-right change.
g8-t2-slope-points.firstStep: Read each point as horizontal coordinate first, vertical coordinate second; check the graph's tick spacing.
g8-t2-slope-points.check: Does your slope's sign agree with whether the line rises or falls from left to right?

g8-t2-slope-triangles.byHand: Form a directed rise-to-run ratio from the origin to each point and compare the reduced ratios.
g8-t2-slope-triangles.calculator: Check only: verify fraction reduction after writing both rise-to-run ratios and identifying the scale factor.
g8-t2-slope-triangles.showWork: Write both slope fractions and show how the same factor scales their numerators and denominators.
g8-t2-slope-triangles.answerForm: Give the common exact slope and explain why scaling both changes preserves the ratio.
g8-t2-slope-triangles.firstStep: For each point, use its change in y from the origin as rise and its change in x as run.
g8-t2-slope-triangles.check: Do both fractions reduce to the same signed value? A downward vertical change must retain its negative sign.

g8-t2-graph-y-mx.byHand: Identify the slope, choose points satisfying the equation, and draw the line through them on the grid.
g8-t2-graph-y-mx.calculator: Check only: verify chosen point values afterward; plot and draw the line by hand.
g8-t2-graph-y-mx.showWork: State the slope, list or label at least three points including the origin, and show one point calculation or slope step.
g8-t2-graph-y-mx.answerForm: Give the exact slope and a straight line across the grid through at least three marked points, including the origin.
g8-t2-graph-y-mx.firstStep: Mark the origin, then read the slope as a signed vertical change over a horizontal change.
g8-t2-graph-y-mx.check: Does each marked point satisfy the equation, and does the line's direction agree with the slope's sign?

g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.byHand: Find the constant output-to-input ratio, write a proportional rule, and substitute the requested input.
g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.calculator: Check only: verify the fraction and substitution after completing them by hand.
g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.showWork: Write the y-to-x ratio from the given point, the equation, and the substitution for the new input.
g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.answerForm: Give the equation with an exact coefficient and the requested output value.
g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.firstStep: A proportional rule has the form y = mx; divide the given output by its input to find m.
g8-t2-proportional-missing-value.check: Does your equation contain the given point and pass through the origin?

g8-t2-intercept-graph.byHand: Read where the line meets the vertical axis and explain that point using both axis labels.
g8-t2-intercept-graph.calculator: No calculator needed; read the labeled scale and interpret the point.
g8-t2-intercept-graph.showWork: Identify the point with zero elapsed time and write a sentence connecting its coordinates to the tank.
g8-t2-intercept-graph.answerForm: Give the y-intercept as an ordered pair and state the starting water amount in liters.
g8-t2-intercept-graph.firstStep: Find zero on the time axis and follow it to the line on the vertical axis.
g8-t2-intercept-graph.check: Does your explanation describe water already in the tank when filling or draining starts, rather than a rate?

g8-t2-intercept-table.byHand: Find the constant rate, work back to zero input, and use the initial output to test proportionality.
g8-t2-intercept-table.calculator: Check only: verify the rate and intercept arithmetic after deriving them by hand.
g8-t2-intercept-table.showWork: Write a rate calculation and either backward steps to zero input or substitution into y = mx + b.
g8-t2-intercept-table.answerForm: Give the y-intercept as an ordered pair and state whether the relationship is proportional, with a reason.
g8-t2-intercept-table.firstStep: Compare two consecutive rows: divide the change in y by the change in x.
g8-t2-intercept-table.check: Does your rate and intercept reproduce every row? Does the resulting line pass through the origin?

g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.byHand: Identify slope and intercept, plot the intercept, and use signed rise and run to locate more points.
g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.calculator: Check only: substitute your plotted points afterward; construct the graph by hand.
g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.showWork: State slope and intercept, mark at least three points, and record a slope step or point calculation.
g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.answerForm: Give the exact slope, the y-intercept as an ordered pair, and a straight line through at least three marked points.
g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.firstStep: Match the equation to y = mx + b and plot the point where x is zero.
g8-t2-graph-slope-intercept.check: Do all marked points satisfy the equation, and did the slope move you in the correct vertical direction?

g8-t2-equation-from-graph.byHand: Use the labeled points to calculate slope, then substitute a point to find the initial value.
g8-t2-equation-from-graph.calculator: Check only: verify your fraction arithmetic or substitute points after deriving the equation by hand.
g8-t2-equation-from-graph.showWork: Write both coordinate differences in the slope fraction, then show substitution and solving for b.
g8-t2-equation-from-graph.answerForm: Give an equation in y = mx + b form with exact, simplified coefficients.
g8-t2-equation-from-graph.firstStep: Read and record both labeled ordered pairs, using the axis scales rather than counting unlabeled spaces.
g8-t2-equation-from-graph.check: Does your final equation produce the plotted y-value for each of the two labeled x-values?

g8-t3-relation-table.byHand: Compare inputs and track every output assigned to each input.
g8-t3-relation-table.calculator: No calculator needed; decide from the input-output pairs.
g8-t3-relation-table.showWork: Identify any repeated input and its outputs, or explain that each input has only one assigned output.
g8-t3-relation-table.answerForm: Answer yes or no and give evidence from the table using the function rule.
g8-t3-relation-table.firstStep: Scan the input column for repeats before examining the corresponding outputs.
g8-t3-relation-table.check: Did you test repeated inputs rather than reject a relation just because an output repeats?

g8-t3-vertical-line-points.byHand: Compare the plotted x-coordinates and apply a vertical-line test to this set of separate points.
g8-t3-vertical-line-points.calculator: No calculator needed; inspect the point coordinates and vertical alignment.
g8-t3-vertical-line-points.showWork: Describe whether any vertical line meets more than one point; identify the input if it does.
g8-t3-vertical-line-points.answerForm: Answer yes or no with a vertical-line explanation. Leave the discrete points unconnected.
g8-t3-vertical-line-points.firstStep: Imagine sliding a vertical line across the plot and count how many points it meets at each input.
g8-t3-vertical-line-points.check: Does your test keep x fixed, and have you considered only the given points?

g8-t3-rule-table-graph.byHand: Substitute every input into the rule, complete the table, and plot and connect the resulting points.
g8-t3-rule-table-graph.calculator: Check only: verify completed output calculations afterward; fill the table and construct the graph by hand.
g8-t3-rule-table-graph.showWork: Write a substitution for each row, label the plotted points, and explain how one row gives its coordinates.
g8-t3-rule-table-graph.answerForm: Complete every table blank, draw the straight line through the points, and explain one row-to-point connection.
g8-t3-rule-table-graph.firstStep: Copy the first input into every x position in the rule, using parentheses if it is negative.
g8-t3-rule-table-graph.check: Is each point's horizontal coordinate the table input and its vertical coordinate the calculated output?

g8-t3-graph-function-rule.byHand: Read the initial output, calculate the slope from the labeled points, and build and evaluate a linear rule.
g8-t3-graph-function-rule.calculator: Check only: verify point substitution and the requested output after deriving the rule by hand.
g8-t3-graph-function-rule.showWork: Write the slope fraction, identify the intercept, write the equation, and substitute the requested input.
g8-t3-graph-function-rule.answerForm: Give the linear equation and the output corresponding to the specified input.
g8-t3-graph-function-rule.firstStep: Record the two labeled points and locate the point whose input is zero.
g8-t3-graph-function-rule.check: Does your equation reproduce both labeled points before you use it at the new input?

g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.byHand: Compare changes in output over changes in input across the whole table.
g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.calculator: Check only: verify your differences after setting up and calculating the rates by hand.
g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.showWork: List all consecutive output changes and their corresponding input changes, then compare the rates.
g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.answerForm: State linear or nonlinear over the shown inputs and support the choice with the calculated rates.
g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.firstStep: Check whether consecutive input values are equally spaced before comparing output differences.
g8-t3-linear-or-nonlinear-table.check: Have you compared every interval, and are your subtractions consistently later value minus earlier value?

g8-t3-compare-function-rates.byHand: Find each function's rate and zero-input output, then make the two comparisons separately.
g8-t3-compare-function-rates.calculator: Check only: verify the table's rate calculation after identifying both rates and initial outputs by hand.
g8-t3-compare-function-rates.showWork: Record each rate and initial output; include a change-in-y over change-in-x calculation for the table.
g8-t3-compare-function-rates.answerForm: Name the function with greater rate, then compare the outputs at zero, allowing equal outputs when appropriate.
g8-t3-compare-function-rates.firstStep: For the equation, distinguish the coefficient of x from the constant; find their matching quantities in the table.
g8-t3-compare-function-rates.check: Did you divide by the actual input change and compare rates separately from starting outputs?

g8-t3-context-linear-model.byHand: Translate starting area and hourly growth into a function, explain both parts, and substitute the requested time.
g8-t3-context-linear-model.calculator: Allowed after writing the function and substitution; use it for the prediction arithmetic.
g8-t3-context-linear-model.showWork: Write the model, label the rate and initial value with units, and show the prediction substitution.
g8-t3-context-linear-model.answerForm: Give the function, both coefficient meanings, and the predicted area in square meters.
g8-t3-context-linear-model.firstStep: Separate the area already finished from the additional area completed after x hours.
g8-t3-context-linear-model.check: At zero hours, does the rule give the starting area? Does each additional hour add the stated amount?

g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.byHand: Use the change in cost per added piece to find the rate, then recover the fixed fee from either total.
g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.calculator: Allowed after writing the cost-change ratio and fee equation; use it for arithmetic while keeping the model on paper.
g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.showWork: Show the difference ratio, substitution into cost = rate times pieces plus fee, and the resulting rule.
g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.answerForm: Give C(x), the setup fee in dollars, and the per-piece charge in dollars per piece.
g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.firstStep: Subtract the two costs and the two piece counts in the same order.
g8-t3-two-values-linear-model.check: Does your function reproduce both given totals, including the fixed fee only once in each total?

g8-t3-square-display-model.byHand: Write both tile-count rules, classify their growth, and set up the total or increase comparison requested.
g8-t3-square-display-model.calculator: Allowed after writing both rules and substitutions; use it for table arithmetic and any new-total-minus-old-total calculations.
g8-t3-square-display-model.showWork: Complete all table rows, explain each classification using equal input steps, and show the requested comparison calculation.
g8-t3-square-display-model.answerForm: Give the completed table, each rule's classification, and which design has more of the requested quantity, or a tie.
g8-t3-square-display-model.firstStep: For each design, separate the tiles that vary with n from the fixed decoration; keep A and B labels attached.
g8-t3-square-display-model.check: Does the prompt ask for total tiles or extra tiles? For extra tiles, compare changes rather than final totals.

g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.byHand: Write both rental cost rules and use their starting fees and hourly rates to explain how the comparison changes.
g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.calculator: Allowed after writing both cost rules and substituting the listed hours; use it to calculate the table entries.
g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.showWork: Show both rules, fill all table cells, compare costs row by row, and state one needed assumption.
g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.answerForm: Give the completed dollar-cost table, explain where the cheaper option changes or ties, and name a reasonable assumption.
g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.firstStep: For each option, add its fixed charge to its hourly rate times the booking length.
g8-t3-rental-comparison-model.check: Did each row use the same hours for both options, and does your explanation agree with every table comparison?

g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.byHand: Read each segment from left to right and decide how the output changes over its time interval.
g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.calculator: No calculator needed; read the time boundaries and compare the endpoint heights.
g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.showWork: For each segment, record its start and end times and whether y rises, stays level, or falls.
g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.answerForm: List the increasing, constant, and decreasing time intervals in minutes and describe the change in y.
g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.firstStep: Mark the time values where the graph changes direction or becomes horizontal.
g8-t3-increasing-decreasing-graph.check: Are your interval boundaries time values? A graph below zero can still increase as its outputs get larger.

g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.byHand: Calculate distance change divided by time change for each interval, then compare the two rates.
g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.calculator: Check only: verify the two rate calculations after reading coordinates and setting up the ratios by hand.
g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.showWork: Write a difference quotient for each interval, with distance and time units.
g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.answerForm: Name the faster time interval and give both rates in meters per second.
g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.firstStep: Record the two endpoint coordinates of each interval; subtract starting values from ending values.
g8-t3-compare-increasing-intervals.check: Did you compare rates rather than ending heights, and does the steeper segment have the greater rate?

g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.byHand: Add successive travel and rest durations to locate transition times, then sketch distance from home over time.
g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.calculator: Check only: verify cumulative times afterward; decide graph directions and draw all segments by hand.
g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.showWork: Write cumulative times, label the starting and transition ordered pairs, and connect them with appropriate straight segments.
g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.answerForm: Give a labeled distance-from-home graph showing the walk away, rest, and return with correct time and distance units.
g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.firstStep: Make a timeline from the start, adding each duration to the time already elapsed.
g8-t3-sketch-walk-rest-return.check: Does distance stay unchanged during the rest and return to zero at home? Use elapsed times, not individual durations.

g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.byHand: Calculate the water added in each interval, keep a running volume total, and sketch the connected segments.
g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.calculator: Check only: verify rate-times-duration products afterward; determine the graph and transition points by hand.
g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.showWork: Show each added volume and cumulative time, then label the starting and all transition points.
g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.answerForm: Give a volume-versus-time graph with labeled transition coordinates and units on the axes.
g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.firstStep: Start with the initial volume at zero time; for each filling interval, add rate times duration.
g8-t3-sketch-filling-rates.check: Does the faster filling rate make a steeper rise, and does shutting the tap leave the existing water in place?

g8-t4-scatter-association.byHand: Inspect the overall point pattern for direction, straight or curved form, gaps, and clusters.
g8-t4-scatter-association.calculator: No calculator needed; use visible patterns and reasoning about what observational data can establish.
g8-t4-scatter-association.showWork: Describe what happens to y as x increases, identify any grouping or curve, and address the causation question.
g8-t4-scatter-association.answerForm: Give a short description of the direction and form, including clusters or no clear association when appropriate, plus a causal judgment.
g8-t4-scatter-association.firstStep: Look across the whole plot from small to large x-values before focusing on individual points.
g8-t4-scatter-association.check: Does your description fit the full plot? Have you distinguished an observed pattern from evidence about causes?

g8-t4-scatter-outlier.byHand: Identify the trend followed by most points, locate a point far from it, and consider whether exclusion is justified.
g8-t4-scatter-outlier.calculator: No calculator needed; read coordinates and compare the point with the main pattern.
g8-t4-scatter-outlier.showWork: Describe the main trend, explain how the unusual point differs, and give a reason for your deletion decision.
g8-t4-scatter-outlier.answerForm: Name the trend, identify the outlier by label and coordinates, and explain whether it should automatically be removed.
g8-t4-scatter-outlier.firstStep: Look for the pattern followed by most observations, then compare points at similar x-values.
g8-t4-scatter-outlier.check: Is the selected point far from the trend rather than merely far from the origin? What evidence would justify deleting it?

g8-t4-construct-scatter.byHand: Plot one separate point for each table row and describe the overall association.
g8-t4-construct-scatter.calculator: No calculator needed; read the axis scales and plot each ordered pair by hand.
g8-t4-construct-scatter.showWork: Plot all six ordered pairs and write a sentence describing direction and form.
g8-t4-construct-scatter.answerForm: Give six unconnected points and a description of any linear, nonlinear, or absent association.
g8-t4-construct-scatter.firstStep: Check how much each tick represents, then move horizontally to x and vertically to y for the first row.
g8-t4-construct-scatter.check: Does every row have one plotted point, with x horizontal and y vertical? Repeated inputs can have separate points.

g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.byHand: Match each plotted input to its table row and compare the plotted output with the listed output.
g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.calculator: No calculator needed; read the vertical scale carefully and compare coordinates.
g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.showWork: Record the mismatched point's label, its plotted output, and the table's output at the same input.
g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.answerForm: Name the incorrect point and give its corrected ordered pair.
g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.firstStep: Choose a labeled point, read its x-coordinate, and locate that same x in the table.
g8-t4-correct-scatter-point.check: Does your correction keep the x-coordinate unchanged and match the table's y-value exactly?

g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.byHand: Set up both model predictions and absolute vertical errors for every observed point, then compare their totals.
g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.calculator: Allowed after writing prediction substitutions and observed-minus-predicted differences; use it for arithmetic and adding absolute errors.
g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.showWork: Fill every prediction and absolute-error cell for all six points, total each error column, and compare the totals.
g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.answerForm: Name the better-fitting model and report both total absolute errors as evidence.
g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.firstStep: Use the first row's x in each model, then subtract each prediction from that row's observed y.
g8-t4-compare-fit-lines.check: Are all absolute errors nonnegative, and have you included all six observations exactly once in each total?

g8-t4-write-fit-line.byHand: Calculate the slope through the specified points, solve for the intercept, and explain the role of a model line.
g8-t4-write-fit-line.calculator: Check only: verify exact slope and intercept arithmetic after deriving the line by hand.
g8-t4-write-fit-line.showWork: Write the coordinate-difference slope fraction, substitute one labeled point, and show how you find the intercept.
g8-t4-write-fit-line.answerForm: Give the line's equation with exact coefficients and explain why useful models can miss individual observations.
g8-t4-write-fit-line.firstStep: Use the two named model points, keeping their order consistent in the vertical and horizontal differences.
g8-t4-write-fit-line.check: Does your equation pass through both named points? Distinguish those model points from the other observations.

g8-t4-model-prediction.byHand: Substitute the requested distance, interpret the coefficient's units, and compare that distance with the observed range.
g8-t4-model-prediction.calculator: Allowed after writing the substitution; use it for the prediction arithmetic and explain the slope and range yourself.
g8-t4-model-prediction.showWork: Write the substituted expression, label the slope's units, and state where the input lies relative to the data range.
g8-t4-model-prediction.answerForm: Give an approximate time in minutes, the slope's meaning, and interpolation or extrapolation with a reason.
g8-t4-model-prediction.firstStep: Identify which symbol means distance and replace it with the requested route distance.
g8-t4-model-prediction.check: Did you classify the input distance against the observed distance range, rather than compare the predicted time with that range?

g8-t4-inverse-prediction.byHand: Set the model output to the requested value, solve for its input, and assess that input against the observed range.
g8-t4-inverse-prediction.calculator: Check only: substitute your solved input into the model after completing the algebra by hand.
g8-t4-inverse-prediction.showWork: Write the target-output equation, each solving step, and the comparison with the observed input range.
g8-t4-inverse-prediction.answerForm: Give the input value, identify interpolation or extrapolation, and state one relevant model limitation.
g8-t4-inverse-prediction.firstStep: Replace y with the given target output, leaving x as the unknown.
g8-t4-inverse-prediction.check: Does your input produce the requested model output, and does your limitation fit its position within or outside the data range?

g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.byHand: Set up the prediction and reason from the data range and setting about causal claims and much larger groups.
g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.calculator: Allowed after writing the substitution; use it for arithmetic while explaining the evidence and limitations yourself.
g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.showWork: Show the prediction substitution, explain the causal judgment, and compare the larger proposed group with observed group sizes.
g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.answerForm: Give an estimated kit count, address the exact causal claim, and explain why the far-out prediction needs caution.
g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.firstStep: Identify the horizontal-axis quantity and substitute the requested volunteer count into the rule.
g8-t4-volunteer-data-model.check: Have you treated the rule as a model rather than a guarantee, and named a limitation connected to the setting?

g8-t4-model-realistic-range.byHand: Set up both time predictions, interpret them as counts, and solve an equation for when the model reaches zero.
g8-t4-model-realistic-range.calculator: Allowed after writing both substitutions and the zero-output equation; use it for arithmetic after showing the algebraic steps.
g8-t4-model-realistic-range.showWork: Show both substituted expressions and the equation-solving steps for zero boxes; explain the later result's meaning.
g8-t4-model-realistic-range.answerForm: Give both numerical model outputs with their hours, explain the unrealistic count, and state the model's zero time in hours.
g8-t4-model-realistic-range.firstStep: Replace x with each requested hour separately, then write a third equation with y set to zero.
g8-t4-model-realistic-range.check: Can each output represent a real box count? Which requested or solved times extend beyond the observed hours?

g8-t4-two-way-counts.byHand: Match each requested group to an interior cell, a column total, or the grand total.
g8-t4-two-way-counts.calculator: Check only: verify the table additions after identifying and recording the requested counts.
g8-t4-two-way-counts.showWork: Identify the row-column intersection and show one addition for the outdoor total and one for the grand total.
g8-t4-two-way-counts.answerForm: Give three labeled participant counts in the order asked.
g8-t4-two-way-counts.firstStep: For a question using and, find the cell where its row group and column preference meet.
g8-t4-two-way-counts.check: Is the joint count no larger than its group totals, and have you counted each participant only once in the grand total?

g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.byHand: Use row and column totals to find missing counts, then use completed counts to fill the remaining totals.
g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.calculator: Check only: verify additions and subtractions after filling the table by hand.
g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.showWork: Write a subtraction or addition for each blank, including the requested nonwalker-and-lunch count.
g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.answerForm: Fill every table blank with a whole-number count and explain how you found the specified group count.
g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.firstStep: Start with a row that has its total and one interior count; subtract to find the other count.
g8-t4-complete-two-way-table.check: Do all rows and columns add to their totals, and do the row totals and column totals give the same grand total?

g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.byHand: Identify the joint count and the comparison group for each part before forming the two percentages.
g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.calculator: Allowed after writing and labeling both count-over-group fractions; keep exact fractional percentages if decimals repeat.
g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.showWork: Write the numerator and denominator for each part, explain each denominator, and multiply each ratio by one hundred percent.
g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.answerForm: Label parts (a) and (b) with exact percentages; reduced fractional percentages are acceptable, with no rounding.
g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.firstStep: Circle the words naming who is included in each comparison group: everyone, one session, or one preference group.
g8-t4-relative-frequency-denominators.check: Does each denominator count only the people named by its comparison group, and does each percentage lie from zero to one hundred?

g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.byHand: Form an outdoor-preference ratio within each session, compare the percentages, and explain why group size matters.
g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.calculator: Allowed after writing each outdoor-count-over-session-total fraction; use it for percentage arithmetic.
g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.showWork: Write both within-group fractions and percentages, compare them, and connect the comparison to association in this sample.
g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.answerForm: Give both labeled percentages, state whether this table shows association, and explain the limitation of raw counts.
g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.firstStep: For each session separately, divide the outdoor count by that session's total.
g8-t4-compare-conditional-frequencies.check: Did you use the same preference for both groups and each group's own total? Account for equal percentages if they occur.
